Question: The midpoints of the four sides of a rectangle are \((-3, 0),\) \((2, 0),\) \((5, 4),\) and \((0, 4).\) What is the area of the rectangle?
Solution:
Connecting the four side midpoints gives a smaller parallelogram whose area is easier to read from the coordinates.

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_8_Q18_solution_official_midpoints.png)

Its bottom horizontal side runs from \((-3,0)\) to \((2,0)\), a length of \(5\). Its top side is at height \(4\). The parallelogram therefore has area \(5\cdot4=20\).

Why is that half the rectangle's area? If the rectangle has side lengths \(w\) and \(h\), each corner triangle cut off by the midpoint segments has perpendicular legs \(w/2\) and \(h/2\). Each triangle has area \(wh/8\), so the four corners together occupy \(wh/2\). The inner parallelogram occupies the other half.

The rectangle's area is consequently \(2\cdot20=\boxed{40}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). The midpoint construction lets us use a horizontal base even though the original rectangle is tilted.
